data.gender_notes: Phalguni is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Phalguni is derived from the Sanskrit word 'phalgun' which means 'bringing forth' or 'producing'. The name is associated with the Hindu goddess Phalguni or Phalguni Devi, who symbolizes the onset of spring and new beginnings. The name is also believed to bring prosperity and good fortune. The name Phalguni carries the meaning “Lady of Spring” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Phalguni usually hope their child will grow to embody lady of spring and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Phalguni total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

It is also known as the month of 'holi' or the 'festival of colours'. This month is celebrated as a time of love and joy, where people come together to play with colours and water, spread happiness, and forget past grievances.

historical_references.context: According to Hindu mythology, Phalguni is the name of the demon king Hiranyakasipu's sister, who was a demoness. She was the mother of Holika, another demon. Holika, who was immune to fire, was tasked with killing her nephew, Prahlada, who was a devotee of Lord Vishnu. However, in the end, it was Holika who was burnt to ashes, and Prahlada was saved. This legend is celebrated as 'Holika Dahan' or 'Chhoti Holi' on the eve of Holi.

modern_usage.modern_context: Phalguni is a Hindu name that is most commonly associated with the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna. This month is celebrated as Holi, the 'Festival of Colors', and Phagwah, the Hindu spring festival. In modern times, Phalguni is seen on various social media platforms, particularly Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook, where people share photos and messages related to these festivals.
